open_points.subject: publish / withdraw an artifact pointer by Cabinet Kernel for the agent
open_points.text: publish an artifact pointer | producer service; the owner for any owner service
open_points.question: When Kernel publishes or withdraws a pointer on the agent's behalf, does Registry refuse a project the session is not granted, as R0-41, R0-46 and R0-47 require for every agent-authority call, and with which failure?
options: add 'Kernel for the agent, on a project its session is granted' to who and 'a project the session is not granted refused' to failure
Kernel publishes only as a producer service, without session confinement
open_points.default_guess: Confine Kernel's publish and withdraw for the agent to the session's granted set and refuse other projects with the same refusal as other agent operations.

open_points.subject: read the latest artifact of a type
open_points.text: read the latest artifact of a type | owner; a service
open_points.question: Does 'a service' include Kernel acting for the agent on any project? R0-46 and R0-47 require a granted-set check on every agent-authority call.
options: Kernel for the agent only on a granted project
owner and trusted services only
open_points.default_guess: Owner, trusted services, and Kernel for the agent on a project its session is granted.

open_points.subject: agent refusals vs non-disclosure of project existence
open_points.text: unknown project refused as not found (list rooms, list artifacts); validate answers `not_found`, `archived`
open_points.question: R0-47 says nothing the agent receives tells it whether a project outside its set exists. For an agent, what do validate, list rooms, list artifacts and the agent projection answer for an unknown project compared with an existing but ungranted one?
options: one indistinguishable 'not granted' answer for both
not_found for unknown and not_granted for ungranted
open_points.default_guess: Give the agent one 'not granted' answer for both unknown and ungranted projects. Only granted projects can answer `not_found` or `archived`.

open_points.subject: agent session identity on Kernel's calls
open_points.text: Registry checks on every agent-authority call, independently of Kernel, that the project belongs to the session's set
open_points.question: Kernel holds one token for all sessions. How does Registry know which session a Kernel call is for, and what stops Kernel naming another session's id? Does Kernel ever call without a session, as itself?
options: Kernel asserts the session id and Registry trusts it
a per-session credential minted at registration
Kernel also has non-agent calls of its own
open_points.default_guess: Kernel names the session on every agent-authority call and is trusted for that claim. This trust is written as an explicit boundary. Every Kernel call carries a session.

open_points.subject: revoking the active project
open_points.text: or the project leaves the session's set
open_points.question: When the owner revokes the session's active project, what becomes the active project? Can 'change the active project' name a project outside the set, and what is refused for an unknown session?
options: active becomes none
refuse revoking the active project until another is chosen
open_points.default_guess: Revoking the active project leaves the session with no active project. Activating a project not in the set is refused, and so is an unknown session.

open_points.subject: request access to a project
open_points.text: request access to a project | Cabinet Kernel for one agent session | ... | —
open_points.question: What happens to a request from a session Kernel never registered? And if the owner grants a project directly while a request is pending, does the request stay pending?
options: unknown session refused
request auto-registers the session
open_points.default_guess: A request from an unknown session is refused. A pending request stays pending until the owner answers it.

open_points.subject: restricted customer and existing projects
open_points.text: no new project or correction of a project may name it
open_points.question: Is a correction of a project that already names a restricted customer refused, for example changing only the object? Does restriction also hold back that project's object address from context and read a project for trusted services?
options: only a correction that newly sets the customer is refused
any correction of such a project is refused
restriction also hides the project's personal_data from services
open_points.default_guess: Only a correction that newly names the restricted customer is refused. The project's object data still flows to services cleared for `personal_data`.

open_points.subject: customer whose relationship has ended
open_points.text: end a customer relationship | owner | the Customer marked as ended on that date
open_points.question: May a new project, or a correction, name a customer whose relationship has ended? Can an ended relationship be resumed? Is ending an already-ended or restricted customer allowed?
options: naming an ended customer reopens the relationship
naming an ended customer is refused
owner action to resume
open_points.default_guess: Naming an ended customer is refused until the owner resumes the relationship with an explicit action. Ending it again returns it unchanged.

open_points.subject: automatic retention erasure
open_points.text: When the applicable period ends, Registry itself erases or anonymises the data
open_points.question: No row carries this system action. What triggers it, what does it leave observable (an audit entry, a status), how does it fail, and who records the lawful ground or purpose that holds data longer (R0-49, R0-52)?
options: add a scheduled 'apply retention' action with an audit entry
owner-confirmed retention action listing what is due
open_points.default_guess: Add a system action that runs periodically and leaves an audit entry per record it handles. The owner records a hold or purpose through an owner-interface action.

open_points.subject: import source and conflicts
open_points.text: the projects of the running instances under the identities they carry
open_points.question: Which instances count as 'running instances' rather than test instances, given that the agent's machine is called a test instance? What is the import's input (a dump file or a live connection)? How are two source instances holding the same id (R0-21) resolved? Is a second import after the 'once' refused?
options: only the VPS instance, as a dump file
several instances, with a conflict between sources refusing the whole import
open_points.default_guess: The owner uploads one export per named running instance through the owner interface. Any id clash between sources or with production refuses the whole import. A second import is refused.

open_points.subject: import of legacy data lacking new required fields
open_points.text: with their customers (`customer_ref` kept), objects, rooms and pointers
open_points.question: v1 data has no Customer kind, no object (only a project address) and maybe `customer_ref`s without Customer records. Is such data refused, filled in during the owner's mapping check, or imported with the missing values left empty?
options: owner supplies the missing values in the mapping
import refused until the source is complete
imported with kind unknown
open_points.default_guess: The owner supplies the missing values (customer kind, object from address) in the confirmed mapping.

open_points.subject: audit log contents vs retention erasure
open_points.text: a project's id is not anonymous by itself (R0-26); the audit log: two years; Otherwise the record is deleted whole (R0-52)
open_points.question: Audit entries name the project, and the id is personal data. When a project is erased under R0-52, do audit entries on it keep the id until their own two-year retention ends? Which operations count as 'significant', including reads of personal_data by services?
options: audit keeps the id under its own retention
audit entries are pseudonymised on erasure
significant = every write and every personal_data read
open_points.default_guess: Audit entries keep the id under their own retention as a stated purpose. Significant operations are every change, every grant or revocation, and every read that returns `personal_data`.

open_points.subject: onboard_object role taken by Kernel flows
open_points.text: its role is taken by the owner interface and Kernel flows
open_points.question: onboard_object created projects, but Kernel no longer creates projects (R0-41) and only the owner creates them. Is onboard_object still a client at all, and with which token? Which part of its role do Kernel flows take?
options: onboard_object is retired; only the owner interface creates
onboard_object keeps a non-creating service token
open_points.default_guess: onboard_object is retired. Creation moves to the owner interface, and Kernel flows only add rooms and pointers on granted projects.

open_points.subject: Capability Box project references
open_points.text: packages carry verifiable project references and source revisions; the receiver checks them
open_points.question: Against what does a receiver verify a project reference and revision? No Registry action returns a revision to a service (validate does not).
options: receiver uses validate only
read a project returns the revision to cleared services
no Registry involvement
open_points.default_guess: The receiver verifies existence through validate, and the revision through 'read a project' with a cleared token.

open_points.subject: Cabinet Web mirror
open_points.text: Each authenticates with its own service token (R0-27)
open_points.question: The actor list says the mirror authenticates with its own token, but R0-27 keeps its read only if it receives one. Does the owner give it a token, and with which operations and class?
options: mirror gets a read-only token without personal_data
mirror loses access
open_points.default_guess: The mirror gets no token until the owner decides. It is listed as a consumer only conditionally.

open_points.subject: standing of R0-45
open_points.text: the owner's answers of 2026-10-27 on its conflicts with that frame are recorded as R0-24 to R0-52
open_points.question: R0-45 is 'proposed to the owner ... no objection', not an owner answer. Is it an accepted owner decision now, or does it wait for the owner's acceptance of the whole?
options: accepted by no objection
pending until State 0 is accepted as a whole
open_points.default_guess: Treat R0-45 as accepted, and confirm it explicitly when the owner accepts State 0 as a whole.
